appearance.organs.flower.shape.rays.why: A head card draws each ray floret of a radiate head as a ray.

appearance.organs.flower.shape.disc.why: A head card draws the disc about as wide as the involucre, with a ray's length beyond it on either side: the disc's share of the head's width.

appearance.organs.flower.shape.clusters.why: An umbel card draws an array's heads as its small flowers, in clusters: as many clusters as heads in each, up to the 30 clusters the card can show.

appearance.organs.flower.shape.florets.why: Each of the card's clusters holds an equal share of the array's heads, up to the 60 a cluster can show.

traits.inflorescence_unit.note: VicFlora's family description: the flowers sit packed on a shared receptacle in heads (capitula), each almost always ringed by an involucre of bracts.

traits.leaf_arrangement.note: VicFlora's family description: leaves one or two to a node, rarely more; it names neither as the usual state.

traits.fruit_type.note: VicFlora's family description: the fruit is usually a cypsela (a one-seeded fruit from an inferior ovary), often topped by a pappus.

rules.note: How PlantGen's cards draw the daisy family's heads, a choice of the model's until heads are built from their florets (spec rework M6): a head card draws one head face on, its rays the ray florets' straps round a disc of florets; an umbel card draws a flat-topped array of small heads, each one of its flowers, the flowers in clusters. A head's width is its involucre's, as floras measure it, plus a ray on either side.
